title: 能塞进书包的 AI 工作站：华硕 ProArt 创 16 RTX Spark 评测｜IGN 中国
text:
相关文章: 一文读懂 RTX Spark：它到底是什么，游戏玩家应该怎么看待？
NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X 的笔记本系列产品已于 10 月 16 日正式上市。
这是黄仁勋口中“PC 的全新开始”，目标是将本地 AI 处理能力、图形创意工作站和游戏中心三大需求合而为一。NVIDIA 还表示，全新架构让续航不再成为 Windows 设备的短板，并具备几乎没有损耗的离电性能。
不久前，我们拿到了一台来自华硕的“ProArt 创 16 RTX Spark”。这几天我认真折腾了一下这台笔记本，也带着它出了两次差，来和大家聊聊实际使用体会。
而有关“RTX Spark 到底是什么”的疑问，有兴趣的读者可以参考我们 此前发布的这篇文章 ，相信能够解决大多数疑问。
综述 & 开箱
我们拿到这台 ProArt 创 16 RTX Spark 是 64G 版本，官方售价 28999 元，128G 版本则是 37999 元。
笔记本的包装比较简洁。我们拿到的是美版，内容物除了 16 寸的机器本体外，还有一枚 140W 的 USB-C 电源（线材可拆卸）、一个内胆包和一枚 ProArt 三模鼠标。但要注意，国行版本并没有附带这枚鼠标。
接下来看看接口。笔记本一共包含 3 个 40 Gbps 满血 USB-C，支持显示输出与 PD 供电；1 个 10 Gbps 的 USB-A，1 个 HDMI 接口，1 个 SD Express 7.0，和 1 个 3.5mm 耳机接口，扩展性能优秀。供电与 MBP 同样采用 USB-C，任何一个接口都可以插电，很方便。
屏幕是 16 英寸 2.8K 120Hz 峰值 1100nits 的 OLED 触控屏，覆盖 100%DCI-P3 广色域，表面配备抗反射涂层，可减少环境反光，观看体验十分出色，符合这台设备的“专业生产力”定位。如果你买的是 128G 顶配版本，那屏幕还会进一步升级到 4K 屏。
硬件配置方面，它搭载了全新的 RTX Spark N1X 芯片，将 20 核 ARM CPU、拥有 6144 个 CUDA 核心的 Blackwell GPU，以及 64GB 统一内存放进了一起。这里的 64GB 是统一内存，由 CPU 和 GPU 共享。内存带宽 300GB/s，让它拥有了运行本地大语言模型的能力，也能跑 3A 游戏。硬盘自带 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD，双 M.2 2280 插槽，具备很强扩容能力。
我们这里多提一嘴它的统一内存：和苹果架构不太一样，RTX Spark 设备允许用户自行手动调节内存与显存各自的占比。以我这台 64GB 版本为例，最多可以将显存调整至 48GB。不过也有比较麻烦的地方：每次调整设置都需要重启。
让我比较意外的是，这台 16 寸的笔记本重量仅为 1.79kg，是华硕迄今为止最为轻便的 16 寸设备。
下图是它的详细配置。
这款 ProArt 16 的表面采用了特殊涂层处理，拥有类似 Macbook 表面的抗指纹防污能力，让整体外观也显得非常精致。
AI 能力实测
RTX Spark 最具野心的领域显然是本地 AI。在这个生活和工作时基本离不开 AI 工具的时代，Token 成了新的核心货币。而本地 AI，一方面能解决 token 的费用问题，另一方面可避免把模型推理和本地文件默认上传至模型云端 —— 但联网搜索、云端模型、插件权限和 Agent 操作范围仍需逐项确认。
这里说明一下：我们执行的任务使用的大模型是本地的，但 Agent 本身工作时是具备联网能力的。也就是说，有必要的话，Agent 会去主动联网验证信息完整性，但并不会将你的对话和交给 Agent 的文件都上传到了云端，用 Agent 来操作剪片子也不用等待本地文件漫长的上传过程。Agent 就是 Hermes、Workbuddy 等智能体，起到手脚的作用，切切实实地动手办事；Qwen、Deepseek、ChatGPT 等大模型是智能体的“大脑”，用什么模型决定了 Agent 的能力上限。
我们来实际看看这台笔记本的 AI 能力和其他设备相比有什么过人之处。
首先是系统层面的兼容。笔记本第一次开机后，就会有类似首次安装 Windows 一样的强引导，只需要简单几次点击就能安装自己的 Agent，首发包含 Hermes、OpenClaw 和 Perplexity 三种，后续还会追加更多。
我们直接安装了 Hermes，并下载了 Qwen 3.8 27B 版本地模型。对 64GB 的统一内存来说，30B 左右的模型正是它的舒适区。
接下来用本地模型试着让 Hermes 下载更新 Windows 中文语言包，并安装 Chrome、Obsidian 等常用软件 —— 非常顺利，几分钟就搞定了，这些软件都已提供了原生 ARM 支持。
我让它根据自己的配置并结合现有公开资料，查询并制作一张 ProArt 创 16 RTX Spark 配置图 —— 就是本文前面用到那张。Hermes 生成了一个 HTML 网页文件，并通过浏览器截图完成了这项工作，并且非常细心地使用了深色底色搭配 #76B900，英伟达绿。
然后换成我们国内用户比较熟悉的 Workbuddy 试试。目前 Workbuddy 也提供了本地模型可供调用，模型推理引擎为 CUDA-13，大小 15.2GB，仅限 Win11+ARM 架构使用，需要至少 32G 内存，是为了 RTX Spark 设备准备的专属本地模型。
这次我让 Workbuddy 执行了一个和 IGN 相关的任务：我截图了我们网站的评分卡，让它做一个类似的 html 版评分卡生成器。
2 分 34 秒后，页面生成。虽然有点小 bug（比如评分数字没居中），但我要求的功能都顺利实现了，甚至还给每个分数都加上了合适的二字评价 —— 这是我忽略的细节，我并没有告诉它每个分数对应什么评语。
为了确定我在 Workbuddy 中安装的本地模型到底消耗了多少 token，我还在 Workbuddy 的指导下安装了一个查看本地模型 Token 吞吐量的 skill。三次对话（首次打招呼、做评分卡生成器、如何查看消耗量）消耗的 Token 总量如下图所示：
NVIDIA 官方还给这套平台准备了一套本地推理的推荐配置，模型、量化格式到启动参数都已写死。用它跑的好处是，至少能保证“英伟达自己也认可这个跑法”。我们按照官方给的参数启动了 llama-server，并写了一个 Python 脚本，分别用短对话、长文档摘要、代码生成和 4K / 32K / 128K 长上下文六组用例，测量了 prefill 速度（读取提示词）和 decode 速度（生成回答）。
本地推理的速度无法用类似 3DMark 跑分的形式直接展现，我们分别概述。Prefill 阶段吃算力，6144 个 CUDA 核心和 FP4 Tensor Cores 在这时候发挥作用；Decode 阶段吃内存带宽，300 GB/s 的统一内存带宽是瓶颈。此外，测试全程开启了 DFlash 投机解码 —— 这也是官方推荐配置的一部分，用一个轻量的草稿模型提前猜测多个 token，再由主模型验证，目的是提升生成速度。
从结果来看，这台 64G 的 RTX Spark 在 Prefill 阶段表现突出：32K 上下文下达到了 18,408 tok/s，128K 下更是超过了 22,000 tok/s —— 意思是喂给它的长文档越多，算力利用率越高。Decode 速度则受限于内存带宽，长文档摘要和代码生成约 5.2 tok/s，长上下文下随着 KV cache 膨胀降至 2.6–2.7 tok/s。作为参考，人类阅读速度大约在 300–500 字/分钟，这个生成速度已经可以满足基本的低延迟交互。
另一个值得关注的数字是 128K 上下文。在 64GB 统一内存的支持下，这台笔记本可以一次性吃进约 49,000 tokens 的超长提示词并完成推理，这也是同级别独显笔记本（通常 8–16GB 显存）根本无法触及的。
以下是本次测试的最终图表。
最后提一嘴笔记本在跑模型时的状态：绝大多数测试我都是在酒店房间内、夜间完成的，在使用本地算力和进行上下文 128k 测试时，能明显听见风扇正在拉满了狂转，类似游戏本在跑 3A 时的噪音，是日常在办公室里无法忽略的程度；温度方面，掌托部分基本没有什么问题，但屏幕转轴附近能明显感受到热量。
续航 & 离电性能
采用 ARM 架构的一大好处就是能耗比会比传统架构更出色。
NVIDIA 工程师此前曾表示，RTX Spark 的离电性能与插电性能差距仅为 1%，几乎可以忽略不计，这对笔记本等移动端设备还是蛮有意义的 —— 用过 Win 掌机的用户应该都能理解我想表达的意思。
将系统离电设置为性能模式后，我在日常使用大模型、办公等环境确实感受不到明显差异。游戏跑分方面，部分游戏甚至离电分数更高，我会在后面的游戏部分单独给出测试结果，但大家测试条件都不太一样，因此结果仅供参考。
至于续航，和我的理想状态确实还有点差距，至少无法达成 MacBook 那种“一天不带电源完全没有电量焦虑”的状态。
这台电脑内置 99.9Wh 大容量电池，刚好是“可随身携带 100Wh 以下设备”的常见门槛，对我这种经常出差的用户来说非常体贴。
日常办公开网页、写稿子、聊微信、看网页视频这种没什么压力的应用场景，以 70% 屏幕亮度、标准模式使用，在实际使用大约 5 小时后电池还剩不到 20% —— 因为飞机当天刚好延误了 6 小时，我对这个续航时间印象蛮深。
但重度使用本地大模型掉电就很快了。不知道各位是否有尝试过在手机上装本地模型：随便聊两句就会明显感觉到手机发烫，且电池百分比也是肉眼可见在迅速降低，用笔记本也是同理。
说回到这台笔记本。llama-bench 满载状态，使用性能模式，屏幕亮度 70%，用脚本拉满本地算力跑了 Qwen 3.8 27B 持续 5 分钟，满电开跑，笔记本电池从 100% 掉到了 92%，预估整体满电续航约 1.1 小时 —— 考虑到这是在跑 27B 参数大模型，这个表现已经相当可观了。
游戏性能 & 跑分实测
作为游戏玩家，我们自然非常关心它的游戏表现。
这台机器采用 ARM 架构，目前未提供 ARM 原生版本的 x86/x64 应用通常通过 Prism 运行；兼容性与性能仍由具体游戏、反作弊和驱动决定。部分游戏如《我的世界》基岩版还提供原生 ARM 支持，甚至跑出 1000 多帧。
由于 Prism 转译主要通过 CPU 完成，DX12、光追、DLSS 这些图形部分原生调用 GPU。因此很多更吃显卡的新作在这台机器上运行良好，而重点考验 CPU 的游戏 —— 比如《刺客信条：影》，The Verge 的测试表示它只能跑个 30 几帧。
网游和竞技类游戏的支持还在推进中。《使命召唤》预计 2027 年正式适配，《英雄联盟》《三角洲行动》等游戏目前已承诺会在后续提供支持（但截至发稿仍然无法运行），《漫威争锋》《DotA 2》《永劫无间》能直接玩，还有更多开发商早已表示会陆续提供支持。
然后看看跑分实测。注意在跑以下测试时，我已经将笔记本的显存手动调整至 48G，其余分配给内存，并在 ProArt Creator Hub 软件中为电脑选择了“性能模式”。
《3DMark》
可以看到图中两项基准测试的离电保持率都在 98% 以上，损耗极低。Steel Nomad Light 考验纯光栅化算力，Solar Bay Extreme 是光追基准，两者的成绩对一台轻薄笔记本来说都还不错。比较强悍的是离电表现 —— 绝大多数笔记本 GPU 离电后都要掉一截，RTX Spark 的分数都几乎没动，统一内存架构在供电策略上确实有优势。
Time Spy 目前仅有 x64 版本，分数被转译拖累，没什么参考价值，这里干脆就跳过了。
《赛博朋克 2077》
《赛博朋克 2077》的测试结果是比较意外。DLSS 4 倍多帧生成开启后，离电 110.66 帧，比插电的 97.63 fps 还要高出 13%。离电分数反而更高，当然很大程度上可能是温度、后台任务进程等细节的差异，但另一方面也说明该场景下未必受 GPU 功耗上限主导；由于开启了 DLSS 4X，不能把显示帧率直接等同于原生渲染性能。DLSS 关掉后，两者基本持平（46.94 vs 47.15），原生渲染下供电模式几乎不影响帧率。
《极限竞速：地平线 6》
具体图形选项和结果参见图片。和 2077 差不多。DLSS 4 倍多帧生成开启时离电 113 帧略高于插电 112 帧，但关闭后差距放大了一点：3K 中画质原生渲染只有 32 帧，离电掉到 30 帧，保持率 93.8% ——《FH6》对原生渲染的负载很高。
《黑神话：悟空》
“黑猴”是这四款游戏里 DLSS 依赖度最高的一款，在其他机器上也是如此。游戏的原生渲染只有 35 帧，开启 DLSS 4X 多帧生成后翻到 83 fps，提升 137%。离电表现也有一定差异：DLSS 开着时保持率 92.8%，关闭后帧数相同，说明黑神话的 GPU 负载在原生状态下还没达到供电上限。
结论就是，即便对竞技类游戏没有强需求，想用 RTX Spark 代替传统游戏本甚至台式机，还是不太现实。游戏适配最多只是它“锦上添花”的功能，而非强项。
结语
RTX Spark 真正的意义，是它第一次把“能认真跑本地大模型”的门槛压进了 1.7kg 级的移动设备。带着它出差时，64GB 统一内存和不错的离电性能，确实让本地 Agent、长文档处理和大模型推理不再只是桌面机房才能完成的任务。
但这台 ProArt 创 16 显然并不侧重游戏性能，Windows on ARM 的游戏适配、反作弊和转译损耗，也决定了它暂时无法取代传统游戏本。近三万元的售价不是所有人都能接受的，续航也的确没能达成竞品的水平。
我更愿意把它理解为一台 NVIDIA 预判未来的产品，或是“提前抵达的工作机”：给那些对本地模型有强需求、又不想把一台高配主机搬来搬去的用户。对更多人来说，RTX Spark 现在未必是最划算的答案，但它已经证明了 PC 平台接下来的发展方向。
本文由 IGN 中国原创撰写，原作者 Zacky Zhang，未经授权禁止转载。

title: 《异界揭踪》试玩前瞻 & 访谈：昭和为背景的搜打撤 RPG｜IGN 中国
text:
相关文章: 《异界揭踪》公布预告
《异界揭踪（ANOMALITH）》是 FURYU 主导企划与发行、Winning Entertainment Group 开发的日式动作 RPG 游戏，预定 10 月 28 日发售，登陆 PS5、Switch 2 与 PC。
虽然看起来是个规模不太大的小成本作品，但参与本作开发的有不少行业大佬：剧本是田中罗密欧 —— 写过《人类衰退之后》《CROSS†CHANNEL》等等，还拿过星云奖提名。角色设计是 MON，西尾维新《传说》系列（不是游戏）的插画师。主题曲由北村友香创作 —— 这个玩家就更熟了，《血源诅咒》《只狼》《艾尔登法环》都有她的参与。
游戏背景设定在类似昭和时代的平行日本，名为“异界”的特殊空间忽然出现，主角水无月玲绪奈为了寻找在异界中失去音讯的挚友，主动加入“特别危险区域对策室”参与调查。
玩法类似传统搜打撤，但是纯单机作品。玩家要操作主角潜入异界，打超常体，搜刮“异物”和物资，并在时限内跑到撤离点。背包空间有限，弹药稀缺，携带物资必然是有限的，这个取舍是整局游戏最实际的压力来源。地图上还分布着“虫洞”，可以把物资直接传回基地，也能当作回城整备的通道。
战斗是枪械和近战的结合。玲绪奈还具备“异形化”能力，这也是游戏的最主要成长要素：吸收异界能量并强化自己的主动与被动技能。在潜入过程中，还会发现可以互动的同伴、供收集的物品线索等等，这也是本作和其他搜打撤最大的不同 —— RPG 要素更丰富一些。
在现场试玩过后，IGN 中国对本作对制作人城所凯（Gai Kidokoro）先生进行了简短访谈。
《异界揭踪》制作人城所凯
IGN 中国：请问游戏的标题具体包含怎样的含义？
城所凯： 我们在命名时，希望能让玩家感受到围绕阈限空间（Liminal Space）的“违和感”与“异常感”，因此选择了这个不太常见的组合。
IGN 中国：《ANOMALITH》为什么会选择昭和日本与阈限空间相结合的主题？这对游戏的世界观和玩法有什么帮助？
城所凯： 这其中有几个原因。我们认为，如果采用传统的恐怖世界观，就很难与其他作品形成差异化，因此决定以昭和时代的日本为基础，融合阈限空间的元素。我认为，这样的主题反而能让不擅长恐怖游戏的玩家更容易接受。
至于为什么选择昭和时代的日本，倒没有什么特别复杂的理由。昭和复古与异界之间并不存在某种必须成立的特殊联系。某些事物会随着时间流逝而呈现出不同的观感：过去习以为常的东西，放到今天来看，反而可能让人感到不安。
比如小时候我的祖母家里有一张小小的阿龟面具，我一直觉得那张面具很可怕。同样，如果一尊古朴的人偶突然出现在身边，可能会让人觉得毛骨悚然；但如果换成一款最新的动漫手办，带来的感受就会完全不同。而昭和复古最容易将这种体验符号化地表现出来，所以我们把它融入了本作的异界设计中。
IGN 中国：作为一款强调异常空间氛围的游戏，本作为什么选择第三人称视角？第一人称视角或许能带来更强的沉浸感。
城所凯： 本作的核心主题，是一名持枪少女在异常世界中求生。如果采用第一人称视角，玩家看到角色的机会就会减少，这个主题也会因此变得不那么突出。所以我们最终选择了更容易观察角色的第三人称视角。
IGN 中国：试玩中我遇到的异化能力相关信息还不多，想请您多介绍更多相关的能力、作用。
城所凯： 异形化技能共有 12 种，其中 9 种是可以强化的技能，剩余3种则是能够改变战局的大招。所有技能都起到辅助枪战的作用，不过其中也有攻击型技能，所以专注攻击型技能的构筑说不定会很有趣。
IGN 中国：异形化能力最初是作为逃生手段，还是攻击手段来设计的？
城所凯： 从设计之初，我们就把它作为攻击手段，也就是枪械射击的辅助。
IGN 中国：如果从游戏中去掉异形化技能，《ANOMALITH》依然可以作为一款枪战 TPS 成立。考虑到部分异形化技能的伤害也相当高，团队认为这套系统不可替代的价值是什么？又是如何平衡技能与枪械的强度的？
城所凯： 实际上，我认为喜欢枪战的玩家，应该也能从本作中获得满足。
我们发现，除了对战类游戏之外，还有很多人并不能从开枪击倒敌人的体验中感受到乐趣。因此，我们设计了既能避免战斗变得单调、又能为枪战增加战术深度的技能。如果从本作中去掉异形化技能，游戏就会变得单调乏味。反过来，我们也很注意调整技能的强度，避免异形化技能让枪械变得没有必要。
IGN 中国：田中罗密欧在本作开发中起到了怎样的作用？能否分享一些合作方面的情况？
城所凯： 从世界观、角色设定到主线剧情，我们都请田中罗密欧先生全面负责创作。他写出了我们所期待的、具有田中罗密欧个人风格的剧本，对此我们非常感谢。
IGN 中国：为什么会邀请北村友香担任音乐制作人？合作过程中有什么值得分享的事情吗？
城所凯： 为了支撑厚重的世界观，我们认为强有力的音乐也是必不可少的，因此需要邀请创作过许多名曲的北村老师。开发过程中，我们把游戏数据提供给她，让她能够实际观看游戏画面并据此进行创作。
本文由 IGN 中国原创撰写，原作者 Zacky Zhang，未经授权禁止转载。

title: 《七龙珠 异战 3》多人模式试玩：战斗激烈程度再升级｜IGN 中国
text:
相关文章: 《七龙珠 异战3》宣传视频 | State of Play
游戏基本信息：七龙珠 异战 3/DRAGON BALL XENOVERSE 3/2027 年/PC、PS5、Xbox Series X|S
《七龙珠 异战 2》发售至今已有将近 10 年时间，作为其特色元素的自定义角色、原创世界观、追求爽快表现的战斗设计还有海量的剧情内容等等，帮助它成为有史以来用户粘性最高的《七龙珠》IP 改编游戏之一，玩家们甚至自发结成社区交流体验。
10 年之后，万代南梦宫于 2026 年 4 月首次公布了这款续作，已故知名漫画家鸟山明生前为游戏创作了全新的龙珠世界“AGE 1000”以及海量原创角色，玩家可以在 6 个种族之间选择自创角色（新追加人造人种族），然后穿梭在西部风格的“AGE 1000”世界里解决各种事件。 还有更多相关内容 《七龙珠 异战3》游戏前瞻
前不久我们试玩了《七龙珠 异战 3》的几个多人对战关卡，虽然时间并不算长，专门为试玩定制的网络环境也出了几次问题，但总的来讲还是能够感受到这款作品在多人联机合作、对战玩法上的基本特色，通过几个很简单的操作就能很顺利地与好友或是陌生人展开一场畅快的合作或对战，战斗过程中的节奏把控也比较到位，哪怕是结束之后感觉耗时比较长的强力 BOSS 战任务，也不会让人觉得拖沓，这一点令人印象深刻。
玩家在“异战 3”中不仅能够和前作一样指定某位原著角色作为自己的老师教导自己战斗能力，而且还新增了灵魂支援以及灵魂交换功能，前者可以在任务中短暂召唤出原作角色进行补刀或提供战力增益，后者则能够消耗一定资源让“导师角色”暂时附身自己，不仅外观可以变成该角色，还能继承其战斗风格以及究极技能。
虽然战斗的主力仍然是玩家自创的角色，但类似另一种“大招”的灵魂交换显然可以给战斗过程带来更多的节奏变化，解锁新的导师之后相当于换了一套大招，而且导师总数超过 130 人，这显然能为玩家提供更充足的游戏动力。
此次试玩能够体验 3 个多人合作 PVE 任务，内容大致相同，只是关底 BOSS 的强度等级不一样，从简单到困难排列分别是 50 名杂兵连战、基纽特战队和吉连、托破组合。玩家进入游戏后首先挑选自己喜欢的自定义角色模组，再从系统预设的 6 套装备中选择一套给角色换上，这样才具备对抗高难度敌人的数值，最后再去 GS 战队基地下层的终端机上选择匹配，等待其他队友完成准备工作，就能组成和前作一样的 4 人小队进入任务。
游戏的操作手感继承了系列一贯的简单、直接、爽快感十足的风格，刚上手的时候可能感觉“发飘”，角色移动速度有些过快，可稍稍适应一段时间就会明白得益于比较强的近战跟踪性能以及慷慨的能量体系，玩家可以抛掉很多顾虑进行释放角色的战斗潜能，轻重攻击的组合与远程发波的伤害接续十分连贯，有时候甚至有种自己的反应跟不上角色敏捷程度的无力感。
当然哪怕是杂兵也不会站在原地白白挨打，在试玩版的任务难度设定下，无论远程还是近战杂兵都有较强的攻击欲望，会主动接近玩家进行合围，偶尔也有从背后发动偷袭把我打一个踉跄的时候，但总的来讲由于 HP 较低并且也基本不会使用闪身、防御等战斗技能，所以基本上无法对玩家构成生命威胁，在游戏中更多扮演的还是 BOSS 出现前让玩家积攒“灵魂交换”大招能量的角色。
整个试玩真正有威胁、让人感觉到游戏难度的 BOSS 只有最后遇到的吉连（恶形）和托破（恶形）。整个任务流程比较长，先要在地下基地各处来回转移清理好几波 HP 不低的小怪和精英，最后能打开研究室的大门遇到二位强力 BOSS。从剧情对话来看，他们都是通过复制罐重现的来自其他宇宙的战士，不知道这些内容是否跟主线故事有关。
这场战斗第一次让我在游戏中感受到了压力，首先两名 BOSS 都拥有一些威力巨大的连招或是大范围发波，稍不注意就会被连续削减大量 HP，此外他们攻防转换的反应速度明显比外面的精英敌人还快，一股脑只管进攻很可能拿不到太大的收益，如果遇到反击技能更是得不偿失。
这时候 4 名队友间的协同能力相比之前的任务就显得尤为重要，先打谁、后打谁，看到敌人蓄力准备反击的时候有没有人提醒及时撤退，如果有人能扮演队长角色进行指挥的话，整场战斗的难度应该会有显著的下降。
但很遗憾跟我一起试玩的都是来自其他国家的媒体，不仅语言不通而且现场也没打开内部语音联络功能，我们 4 人一会儿打这个，一会儿打那个，很快就被两名 BOSS 各个击破，耗尽复活次数导致任务失败。
“灵魂交换”的变身动画相当酷炫
但即便如此，这场战斗还是充分展现了本作在战斗表现力以及多人玩法深度方面的潜能，也从另一个角度论证了这并不是一款单靠无脑操作就可以轻松通关的游戏，虽然不如其他格斗类《七龙珠》游戏那么硬核，看上去有些花里胡哨，但它依然相当程度上继承了“龙珠格斗”的设计精髓，玩家的操作与战斗思路依然扮演着不可或缺的角色。
总结
很遗憾此次试玩并没有体验到任何与剧情任务相关的内容，据官方介绍故事模式通关时间大约 25 小时，玩家将在前作结尾之后 200 年的全新世界里作为“GS战队（超级赛亚超人战队）”的一员展开冒险，本作无论结构、内容还是表现力，相比前代都有长足的进步，期待它也能成为一款在很长时间里持续吸引玩家关注和参与的作品。
本文由 IGN 中国原创撰写，原作者 Kamui Ye，未经授权禁止转载。

title: 《ONE PIECE 海洋盛宴》试玩前瞻：别出心裁的另类演绎｜IGN 中国
text:
相关文章: 《ONE PIECE 海洋盛宴》试玩前瞻：双厨狂喜｜IGN 中国
游戏基本信息：ONE PIECE 海洋盛宴/ ONE PIECE: Grand Gourmet/2026 年 10 月 23 日发售/PC、NS、NS2、iOS、安卓
注：所有译名以游戏实际内容为准。
除了原创的各种题材，开罗社（Kairosoft）曾在 2024 年推出一款广受好评的联动作品《哆啦 A 梦的铜锣烧店物语》，通过将原著中的海量元素与自家擅长的像素模拟经营系统相结合，制造出一种十分独特的游戏氛围，成功吸引到大量粉丝的关注。 还有更多相关内容 《海贼王 海洋盛宴》公布预告 | 任天堂直面会
而计划在 2026 年 10 月 23 日推出的《ONE PIECE 海洋盛宴》毫无疑问是这种开发思路的延续，这一次草帽一伙面对的问题不是战斗、探险、揭露阴谋，而是如何能让自己的海上餐厅吸引更多的食客。
开罗社标志性的高品质像素美术结合超过 400 位各色 NPC、故事彩蛋、场景、道具，共同组合成了一幅乍一看有些荒诞，但仔细观察之后又发现好像处处都合理的神奇画卷。游戏本身也继承了一贯的放置类经营玩法，通过几个很简单的操作，再遵循一些基本规则，就能让餐厅顺利运转起来。
并且游戏的内容十分丰富，按照正常流程简单体验也好，认真挖掘那些不起眼的细节也好，随随便便就能玩上几十个小时根本不会腻，“量大管饱”这一块开罗社绝对不会让人失望。我个人除了对 PC 版照搬手机版 UI、部分简中翻译有些读不懂这 2 点比较不爽以外，其他部分基本持好评态度。
提升评价，吸引 NPC 到店
整件事情当然还是有一个可有可无的起源，以说明草帽一伙为什么中断了伟大航路的冒险回来开餐厅 —— 山智和路飞因为遭遇暴风雨和伙伴走散，结果意外发现山治曾经工作过的海上西餐厅芭拉蒂与另外一艘餐厅船起了冲突，原来是对方是顶着芭拉蒂餐厅招牌招摇撞骗的一伙冒牌货，专门靠价格高品质差的料理宰客，从而降低了芭拉蒂餐厅的评价。
为了教训这伙人，帕迪不顾卓夫的反对驾驶芭拉蒂二号船出海，与冒牌货起冲突时正好被山治和路飞撞见，但却阴差阳错地让对方逃走了。山智显然无法放任不管，于是决定和路飞一起好好经营芭拉蒂二号船，以维护餐厅的名声和评价，同时借机教训一下冒牌货。
具体的游戏流程以类似关卡的“海域”形式展开，每一个海域里都有完全不同的主线成就，全部达成之后就会触发与冒牌货的料理对决，只要战胜它们就算是完成了在该海域的经营，这时可以前往下一个关卡，也可以选择继续经营以积攒更多的货币、金币或是爱心这些资源。
具体的经营方式脉络十分清晰，体现出一种经过多年沉淀的稳定感：呈四边形的芭拉蒂二号甲板就是餐厅的内部空间，有几个默认的基本设施，比如玄关等待处、厨房、一张餐桌。
拿到初始经费之后首先需要消耗食谱素材研发新的料理，食谱包括主菜、副菜、饮料、甜品 4 种，每一种下面又分成肉类、谷物、蔬菜等等品类，而这些食材主要来自派遣路飞和其他团队成员外出冒险的成果，随着海域的不断变化，食材种类本身的变化并不大，但却会不断发明出新的料理。
试吃环节的小彩蛋：路飞面前会有 9 份食物，其他人都是 1 份
新料理发明出来之后首先会让草帽一伙的成员试吃，根据对该项菜式喜好的不同，大家能够获得高低各异的经验值，攒满进度条就能提升一级。草帽一伙成员的等级主要与海兽类怪物招募、战斗能力有关，平常还是不能过于忽视，否则可能会错失一些招募特定 NPC 的机会。
这里必须要提到的是，这些冒险海域的每一个都和原著故事有着非常紧密的联系，NPC、食材、料理类型、突发事件以及这些 NPC 与草帽一伙的剧情对话全都按照原作的时间顺序进行编排，这对我这种看了几十年的老粉来说实在是过于亲切和感动了。
比如游戏的第一个海域显然取材自故事早期的“东海”，在这里你会遇到阿龙、克里克一伙以及其他在原作中出现过的各种 NPC 角色。当然，不管在原作中的情节如何，游戏里这些人全都是来餐厅消费的食客，系统会自动把他们送过来，点单、制作、送达等等全都是自动运行的，不需要玩家亲自操作，只需要不断研发出新的料理并组合成套餐即可。
食客消费之后自然会产生金钱或是餐厅评价收益，同时还会提出各种各样符合他们在原作中身份、情节的要求，满足这些要求往往能获得一些奖励，同时还可能召集他们的好朋友到店享用美食，从而让餐厅的收益不断增加。
一个海域内的 NPC 大约为 40 名左右，全都来自原作并且大致都会按故事发展的顺序到店，当然也不排除提前达成一些先决条件之后提前解锁一些 NPC 的情况出现。尤其需要注意的是这些 NPC“成为粉丝”的条件，只要成为店铺粉丝，哪怕之后餐厅转移到新的关卡去，这些 NPC 也会跨越地区限制继续为店铺提供收益。
赠送特殊的礼物、店铺里有特定的料理或特定设施都可能满足某位 NPC 成为粉丝的条件，不过考虑到 NPC 的数量和条件类型十分多样化，基本上很难挨个记住，只有在礼物页面能看到某些礼品上有“！”标记，说明这件物品对某位 NPC 有特殊的意义，赠送之后要么可以获得丰厚的收益，要么直接成为餐厅粉丝。
“外出冒险”也是游戏里一个跟原著贴合十分紧密的有趣系统，玩家可以派遣路飞+一名草帽一伙成员通过消耗一定的资源前往该海域里的某个特定地点进行自动冒险，途中可能获得食材、菜谱、各种礼品道具以及遇到特殊事件，比如初始海域里可以前往风车村、哥特岛、谢尔兹镇等等，路飞在冒险时也可能解锁与这些地点对应的 NPC，从而把他们发展成食客。每个地点有完成度的概念，有时候需要带领特定的伙伴前往才能解锁全部的事件。
部分在原作中戏份较多、比较重要的食客会专门发来信件要求送去包含特定要求的料理，比如美味度达到 XX 级的甜品、面包类料理之类的，满足之后他们就会成为食客，这也是解锁特定 NPC 的重要手段。另外还有一些 NPC 则需要触发招待事件之后消耗红心资源邀请他们来餐厅吃饭，但如果用餐满意度没有达到他们的要求，也是不会解锁成为食客的。
这就涉及到本作的餐厅布置系统，乍一看似乎种类繁多，让人摸不着头脑，但至少在游戏中前期由于装潢、道具类型有限，基本不用考虑得太复杂，每张餐桌之间留出一定的空间以便插入足够种类和数量的装饰道具来提升餐桌舒适度，然后再按部就班地研发料理、同时注意会受地板影响的“餐桌种类”，其他基本上就没什么操作空间了，一切都是自动运行的。
比较特殊的只有“餐桌种类”这个条件，通过剧情解锁新的地板类型之后，如果铺设的范围内有餐桌，该餐桌就会变成与地板类型相匹配的风格，比如甲板风格、海军风格、阿拉巴斯坦王国风格等等，其他诸如吊扇、屏风、照明灯等等也都有各种各样不同的风格，这除了在外观上能让餐厅内部的装潢更加多变，也会让部分 NPC 的用餐满意度更高，还是一些特殊的 NPC 解锁的必要条件。
正如前面所说，搞清楚一些很基本的原则之后，整个餐厅就会自己运作起来，当然需要玩家进行的操作还是很多的，因为不断会有 NPC 提出新的要求，你也得不断研发新料理、拓展餐厅面积、布置新的设施、以便让食客的满意度始终保持在高位，争取获得更多的粉丝。
总的来讲餐厅的运营工作需要进行的操作很多，但并不会特别费心思，整个系统始终保持着很高的运行效率，不需要我操心太多事情，更多精力可以放在欣赏数百位 NPC 的逗趣像素造型，以及重温那些熟悉的地点、道具、故事上，对于身为几十年原著老粉的我来说实在是非常享受。
至于那些更倾向于体验模拟经营乐趣的玩家来说，这款游戏当然也不会让大家失望，你可以更精细地安排餐厅里的动线、用餐区域分配、装潢风格、设施分布，这些都可以有效提升运营的效率，帮助餐厅更快达成各种主线、支线目标。
达成海域主线条件后与冒牌货的料理对决
本作以游戏内的时间 51 天为期，到期后将会根据玩家的进度和成绩进行分数结算，正常来讲当然是以解锁更多 NPC、达到更高分数为目标，但我个人认为单纯将这款游戏看做是一次与《航海王》原著的另类再相遇，重头以轻松、诙谐的形式梳理一遍路飞从东海开始的这场跨越几十年的冒险，似乎也没什么问题。
从之前官方放出的素材来看，已经能看到洛基等角色的身影，说明游戏里的故事也发展到了巨人之国艾尔巴夫篇，和最新连载的进度相差并不太大，如果是对《航海王》本身的故事、人物、事件有特殊感情，同时又是开罗社像素模拟经营玩法老粉的玩家绝对不要错过这款作品。
本文由 IGN 中国原创撰写，原作者 Kamui Ye，未经授权禁止转载。

title: NOVA海外独立游戏见闻 Vol.157
text:
Vol.157（10 月第 3 周）
本期见闻覆盖时间：10 月 12 日至 10 月 18 日
本期整理： dxmi
行业见闻录
BAFTA 向 112 位创作者提供超 27 万英镑的资助
10 月 12 日，BAFTA（英国电影与电视艺术学院） 宣布 ，其通过 2026 年威廉王子 BAFTA 资助金及奖学金项目，向英国和北美的 112 名受助者提供了总额超过 27 万英镑的资助。这两个项目旨在支持游戏、电影和电视行业的新兴创作者，为他们提供资金及实际帮助，助力其职业发展。
威廉王子 BAFTA 资助金项目面向英国创作者，提供最高 2000 英镑的资助，用于支付培训、设备、软件、搬迁等必要开支。而奖学金项目则面向英国和北美的学生，提供 1.2 万英镑或 6 万美元的资助。BAFTA 的调查显示，在 2024 年和 2025 年获得资助的人群中，98% 的受访者表示，这笔资助帮助他们获得了原本无法把握的职业机会；另有 88.2% 的受访者表示，获得 BAFTA 资助金显著增强了他们在行业中探索和发展的信心。
BAFTA 副主席 Hilary Rosen 称：“BAFTA 始终坚信，投资新生代人才至关重要，因为整个行业的未来都依赖于他们的发展。威廉王子 BAFTA 资助金及奖学金项目正是为此而设——向新兴创作者提供可能改变人生的资助，帮助那些原本可能无缘进入影视艺术行业的人实现职业理想。我们很高兴能够公布 2026 年获资助者名单，也十分期待看到他们未来取得的成就。”
奖项创始人与部分受助者的合影/图片： BAFTA
《s&box》将改为免费模式并调整发展方向
10 月 13 日，Facepunch Studios 创始人 Garry Newman 在 官网 发布文章称，计划在今年年底将《s&box》改为免费模式，并调整平台的发展方向：不再追求尽可能多的游戏数量，而是着力推广最优秀、最受欢迎的作品。已经付费购买《s&box》的玩家将获得专属 Steam 库存物品作为补偿，以 20 美元而非 10 美元购买游戏的玩家还将获得额外奖励。
《s&box》是《Garry's Mod》的精神续作，制作组最初希望将其打造成一个现代、直观且支持模组的游戏开发环境。创作者可以使用《s&box》制作游戏并直接在《s&box》内部发布，也可以将最终成品作为独立作品在 Steam 上发行。然而《s&box》在今年 4 月正式发售后，一直因充斥低质内容而饱受批评。
作者 Garry Newman 在文章中称，已意识到《s&box》“并不受欢迎”，用户留存率也“不理想”。他承认，Facepunch 此前一直专注于引擎本身及开发体验，但现在必须认识到：“我们卖的不是游戏引擎，而是一款游戏。”他表示自己曾设想打造一个“游戏界的 Netflix”，但这种模式最终导致了低质作品的泛滥。《s&box》 应当转变为“一个汇集最优秀、最受欢迎游戏的平台”，并将“良好的品味和出色的观点”置于一切之上。
图片： sbox.game
IGN Fan Fest 2026 秋季版举办
10 月 14 日， 媒体 IGN 举办了 IGN Fan Fest 2026 秋季版线上直播活动，共有 23 款游戏参与。
IGN Fan Fest 是由 IGN 举办的线上展示活动，除了游戏，活动还会带来大量与电影、电视剧和动漫作品相关的独家发布内容。大量独立游戏参与了本次展示，除了《苍穹浩瀚：奥西里斯重生》等已经广受期待的游戏外，还有包括《Trollheim: Gnomes》和《4 Penny Coffins》在内的多款独立游戏首次亮相。
图片： IGN
《毁灭公爵 3D》关卡设计师 Richard "Levelord" Gray 离世
10 月 14 日，Apogee Entertainment 于 社交媒体 宣布，传奇关卡设计师 Richard "Levelord" Gray 已于 10 月 12 日离世，享年 68 岁。
Richard Bailey Gray 曾在 1996 年由 Apogee（当时更名为 3D Realms）发售的《毁灭公爵 3D》担任关卡设计师，游戏发售后，他从 Apogee 离职并参与创立了 Hipnotic Interactive（后更名为 Ritual Entertainment）。除了《毁灭公爵 3D》，他还参与了《雷神之锤》、《半衰期：针锋相对》与《反恐精英：零点行动》等经典 FPS 游戏的关卡设计工作。
Apogee 在讣告中写道：“从《毁灭公爵：3D》中传奇般的作品到无数受他鼓舞的玩家与开发者，Richard 留下了永恒的遗产。”
R.I.P/图片： Twi/X
Steam 推出“成就集合”功能
10 月 16 日，Steam 官方 发布公告 称，旨在改善游戏成就体验的新功能“成就集合”现已进入测试阶段。开发者可以为自己的游戏创建成就集合，玩家也可以在已添加支持的游戏中体验这一功能。此外，成就页面也得到了更新，其搜索功能得到了扩展，并允许玩家与最多三名好友比较成就进度。
现在的游戏时常通过新的 DLC、扩展包和赛季进行更新。然而，随新的游戏内容而添加的成就可能难以被发现，还可能破坏玩家的全成就状态。“成就集合”这一功能允许开发者将成就并入一个个分组，例如将其分为单人集合和多人集合，或将游戏成就划入 8 个以职业区分的集合。
玩家游玩游戏时，仍然会像往常一样获取成就。但游戏成就列表将按开发者创建的成就集合进行划分，每个成就集合都有自己的进度条，显示玩家在本集合内的完成情况。当玩家解锁了某个成就集合中的所有成就后，就会在个人资料中添加一个“集合已完成”奖杯。如果日后有新成就添加到该成就集合中，玩家的全成就达成状态依旧会得到保留。开发者可以创建新的成就集合来容纳属于新增内容的成就。这些新成就集合能让回归的玩家轻松查看可以解锁的新内容，同时为他们保留先前的成就达成状态。
成就集合/图片： Steam
Nvida 下架 RTX 5090 系列显卡
10 月 10 日，媒体 Tom's Hardware 收到爆料 ，称 Nvida 将停产 RTX 5090 系列显卡。尽管 Nvida 官方并未回应这一消息，但从 10 月 15 日开始，各零售商便开始陆续下架 RTX 5090 系列显卡，Nvida 官方商城 也无法再搜索到任何 RTX 5090 系列的售卖选项。
由于 AI 浪潮，显卡价格从去年开始一路飞涨。而据爆料称，Nvida 计划将 RTX 5090 使用的 GB202 芯片全部用于专业显卡和数据中心，这也是为什么 RTX 5090 将会停产。爆料还提到 Nvida 将会推出 24 GB 显存版本的 RTX 5080 以替代现有的 16 GB 显存版本的 RTX 5080。
已无法再搜索到 RTX 5090 的 Nvida 官网/图片： Nvida
The MIX Fall Game Showcase 线上发布会举办
10 月 16 日， The MIX Fall Game Showcase 线上展示会正式开始，超过 60 款独立游戏参与了此次时长将近 2 小时的线上发布活动，活动的 Steam 页面也已同步上线。
大量独立游戏在本次活动中发布了新内容，除了游戏预告与实机演示，《Deadhand Theater》等游戏还同步推出了免费试玩。
图片： Steam
Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 新增 4 个国家展馆
10 月 16 日， 媒体 GamesIndustry 报道 ，Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 2026 宣布将增设 4 个国家展馆，新增展馆分别来自印度尼西亚（创意经济部）、日本（JETRO）、马来西亚（MDEC）和美国（美国驻曼谷大使馆）。至此，本届展会的国家展馆总数达到 20 个，覆盖亚洲、欧洲和北美的 12 个市场。
本届 Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 将于 10 月 29 日至 11 月 1 日在泰国曼谷举办，这是东南亚地区规模最大的游戏行业展会。来自 29 个国家和地区的参展商将参加本次展会，主办方称这将是该展会历史上“国际化程度最高的一届”。
game（德国游戏行业协会）总经理 Felix Falk 在采访中称：“这里是游戏行业东西方交流的交汇点。对于亚洲开发者来说，这是接触国际合作伙伴最直接的途径；对于西方工作室而言，这则是进军全球增长最快的一些游戏市场的门户。”泰国游戏协会会长 Kittipong Prucksa-aroon 表示：“作为东道国行业协会的代表，我们期待与印度尼西亚、马来西亚和菲律宾等其他东盟主要国家的展馆携手，在 Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 汇聚整个地区的游戏产业力量。”
图片： gamescom
“类数独”游戏持续推出线下实体书
线上“类数独”游戏 《Murdoku》 将于 10 月 29 日推出线下实体书《Murdoku: Around the World》，这已经是该系列的第三本线下实体书。尽管该作有免费的线上版本并允许玩家自行打印实体版，但该系列的实体书仍然在持续发行。
在《Murdoku》中，玩家需要根据场景信息和人物描述，推测人物在场景中的正确位置。虽然“类数独”这一类型在整体上略显小众，但一直有稳定的爱好者群体。大部分此类游戏，如 《Murdoku》 和猫猫风格的 《Meowdoku》 都选择了在网页端免费发布，玩家随时都能方便地进行游戏。
图片： Murdoku
独游公告板
一周拾遗 ：本周值得关注的新发售、重新上架或公布新版本的独立游戏。
1. 10 月 14 日，由 Funselektor Labs 制作的《越过山丘 over the hill》正式发售，仅两天就在 Steam 平台获得超 1000 条评价并达到“特别好评”。梦回越野黄金年代，探索广袤无垠天地。驾驶 60 至 80 年代的经典四驱车型，穿越充满挑战的崎岖小径。无论独自出发还是好友同行，都能悠然驰骋，尽情欣赏一路的壮美风光。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2929250/_over_the_hill/
2. 10 月 14 日，由曾经《啪嗒砰》系列开发者所组建的独立工作室 Ratata Arts 的众筹作品《Ratatan》发售了 1.0 正式版，本作延续了《啪嗒砰》系列独特的用音乐指挥的战斗风格。这是一款融合了节奏跟横轴动作，可以最多四人一起合作的 Roguelike 节奏动作游戏。有 100 只以上的角色一起展开激烈的大乱斗。伴随着充满动态节奏感的 BGM 一起打败敌人吧！
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2949320/Ratatan/
3. 10 月 15 日，由 Keen Games GmbH 开发的《雾锁王国》结束抢先体验阶段，发布 1.0 正式版。《雾锁王国》是一款单人/合作生存动作 RPG，在这里，你的自由与创造力将被摆在第一位。竭尽全力战胜蚕食薪谷王国的腐化瘴气：探索手工打造的瑰丽世界，揭开隐藏的秘密并披荆斩棘开辟道路，在完全支持地形改造的世界中尽情建造。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1203620/_Enshrouded/
开发追踪： 本周更新开发关键节点、尚处在开发早期或中期的独立游戏。
1. 10 月 13 日，由 Black Hand 开发，融合了黑暗奇幻与西部风格的《The Dark West》公布新预告片。这是一款黑暗秘术西部 ARPG，故事发生在一片濒临死亡、被腐化吞噬的边疆。使用符合时代背景的武器与黑暗魔法，在致命遭遇中奋力求生，并发掘各具特色的强力物品。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3574750/The_Dark_West/
2. 10 月 14 日，由 Cat Pounce Game Production 开发，专注于机甲战斗体验的《锻钢之心：边陲》发布首个宣传片。《锻钢之心：边陲》是一款以机甲战斗为核心的科幻动作游戏。玩家将扮演雇佣兵驾驶员伊万，与一台拥有「机魂」的军用机甲并肩作战。这颗名为眠龙星的边陲星球蕴藏着奇妙而稀有的矿藏——当豺狼被矿藏引来，你与机魂的选择将决定这颗星球的命运。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4489960/_/
3. 【开发者投递】10 月 16 日，由 Bag Track Games 制作的《Deadhand Theater》在 MIX Fall Showcase 上发布了全新预告，并同步上架免费 Demo。这是一款黑暗风格的回合制 Roguelike 牌组构筑游戏，扑克牌型是你的武器，而你自己的傀儡身体也可以被随意献祭。撕下一只肢体换取绝境中的优势，打磨你的卡组，再多撑过一场战斗。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4650720/Deadhand_Theater/
4. 【开发者投递】10 月 16 日，由芬兰独立工作室 Aulot Games 开发的《Palisade》宣布将为游戏正式版本追加创意工坊和局域网功能，并确定正式版本将于 11 月 10 日发售。在即时战略战场上直接指挥领土，无需微操编队。扩张边界、连通补给道路，并用骑兵突击和海上登陆突破敌阵。包含五段历史战役、遭遇战、内置地图编辑器以及支持最多 8 名玩家的在线多人游戏。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4993270/Palisade/

1. 《天祝我也》
关键字：动作类 Rogue、迷宫探索、动漫；天命不予，我便自取。《天祝我也》是一款赛璐璐动画风格的 3D 动作 Roguelite 游戏。你将扮演人造少女魔法师“莉莉”，孤身闯入一座危机四伏的迷宫。通过掌控水、火、风、地四大元素，收集失落的“加护”，在无尽的变数中磨炼意志。探索、挑战、成长，在这个充满未知与危险的世界中，追寻属于你的命运吧！
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3530630/_/
2. 《STARHOME》
关键字：基地建设、动作即时战略、太空；指挥这支承载着文明幸存者的星舰舰队。合理分配每艘飞船的有限空间，在居住区、生产、防御和武器之间找到平衡。探索银河，在压倒性的威胁下寻找避难之地与生存的希望。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1252070/STARHOME/
3. 《再拆亿包！》
关键字：休闲、整理、收集马拉松；一款单人放置游戏，让你撕开卡包，收集卡牌，完成究极收藏。卖掉重复卡牌，升级装备，然后继续抽卡，并且抽得更快、更多！享受撕开包装，填满卡册，逐渐集齐一切所带来的巨大满足感。该集卡了！
https://store.steampowered.com/app/5088440/_/
4. 《GRAVHOUNDS》
关键字：合作、第三人称射击、动作类 Rogue；这是一款可供 1-4 名玩家合作游玩的动作建造游戏。你们将共同降落至敌对星球，应对遵循真实物理法则的混乱场面，建造并守护基地，并要在沦为外星人的食物之前，尽可能地带着所有物品撤离！坚守的时间越久，危险就越大……但奖励也越丰厚。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2440760/GRAVHOUNDS/
5. 《Alien Archeologist》
关键字：冒险、采矿、清洁；《异星考古学家》是一款轻松悠闲的增量挖掘游戏。使用各式各样可以升级的工具开采矿石、破土掘进、清扫古怪文物，一路向下深入，逐步接近藏在行星核心的秘密。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4881130/Alien_Archeologist/
6. 《Gate Guard Simulator》
关键字：模拟、中世纪、黑色喜剧；穿上城堡卫兵的靴子。查验印章，揪出走私犯，揭露女巫。谁能进门、谁被拒之门外，都由你说了算。你会秉公执法，还是为了一己私利而破例？
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4111570/Gate_Guard_Simulator/
7. 《Gravity Circuit 2》
关键字：动作、平台游戏、复古；一座全新的“方舟”已然崛起。在这款灵感源自经典主机作品、充满火爆战斗的 2D 平台游戏中，你将化身为重力回路或动力回路，这两位均是拥有不凡身手的战士。《重力回路 2》正是广受好评的佳作《重力回路》的正统续作。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3447460/Gravity_Circuit_2/

【招募】《启动流程》寻找美术合作者｜横版类银河城 · 2D / 2.5D
来自： 游戏开发组
会员： yzsdr
《启动流程》是一款正在重制的横版类银河城探索解谜游戏。
项目最早由三人团队完成于 2026 网易 MINI-GAME 比赛，已经有一个时长约 50 分钟，可完整游玩的 UE 版本。比赛结束后，我继续独立开发这个项目，现在已经迁移到 Unity，准备在原型基础上重新制作。
我主要负责游戏设计、系统与关卡、程序，以及叙事设定，这方面经验较充分。现阶段比较缺的是视觉这一侧，所以想找一位美术合作者，从重制早期开始一起确定它最终应该长什么样。
目前的设计拆解、可玩版本、演示和我的其他作品见下：
设计拆解（详细机制&世界观）
可玩版本（itch.io）
演示视频（bilibili）
Portfolio（个人介绍&其它作品）
关于游戏
世界设定
主角是一个无限自我嵌套的方盒机器人。
每一轮，玩家作为"启动子"，在沉睡的更大的自己体内探索，执行它的"启动流程"；被启动的那个更大的自己，就是下一轮的主角。
核心玩法
传统类银河城随着能力/道具的永久解锁，地图可达性按层次逐级扩展。
但《启动流程》不同。玩家逐渐获得的是对更大自己以什么状态启动的调控权限。
主角有载荷、导电、磁性三项性质，每项有两种状态，共组成 8 种启动配置。不同配置会改变主角与环境的交互方式，也因此改变地图的可达关系：一种配置能通过一些路线，同时会失去另一些路线，没有一种配置始终更好。
配置只能在“启动”时重新选择。每一轮，玩家决定下一轮以什么配置、从哪个已经发现的启动点出发；进入这一轮之后，就只能在这个状态下继续探索。有些路线无法一次完成，需要先以一种配置到达新的启动点，再在之后的循环中换一种配置继续前进。
随着地图和启动点逐渐展开，玩法会从局部机关慢慢转向更大尺度的路线规划：从哪里开始、这一轮采用什么配置、在哪里结束，以及怎样把几个循环连接成一条完整路线。
同时，一些机关会在循环结束时复位，部分目标也要求在同一轮内完成跨地图激活和验证。这使玩家不能把所有路线无限拆开，而需要同时考虑循环之间如何衔接，以及这一轮内哪些事情必须连续完成。
空间与视觉
这些玩法发生在一个连续的大型机械空间里，即更大自己的体内。
地图中既有较窄的检修区域和机制空间，也有贯穿多个区域的巨大竖井、跨区结构，以及更大层级自己的外部结构。空间尺度和区域之间的连接不只是背景，也会直接参与路线和机关设计。
原型阶段的美术主要用于支撑玩法和地图，目前还没有形成正式版本的视觉体系。
目前比较确定的是，希望世界整体偏冷、有秩序，强调尺度、大形体、光影和结构关系。

希望找到的合作者
不太限定具体职位名称，2D / 3D / TA 等均可。
比较看重：
对空间、构图和尺度有感觉；
有一定的风格化处理能力；
愿意从灰盒、玩法和地图结构出发讨论视觉；
对环境设计、整体视觉语言感兴趣。

如果你的能力不完全落在这里，但对项目方向感兴趣，也可以聊一聊。

重制现在还在比较早的阶段，所以不会一开始就进入大量正式资产制作。
前期更可能先选几个典型房间和大尺度场景做视觉探索，尝试 2D / 2.5D 两种形式在实际游戏里的效果；然后重新看主角、环境和机关之间的视觉关系，逐渐确定形体、材质、光影、色彩和细节密度；最后做出一个相对完整的典型区域，看看能否支撑后续制作。

title: DLSS Swapper now lets you update all your upscalers in multiple games at once, adds Nvidia's new Frame Generation Preset C
text:
DLSS Swapper just became even more useful, as the upscaler-switching software has rolled out a bulk DLL swapping feature in the latest update.
Version 1.2.7.0 adds a Bulk Swap button to the top right hand menu. Click on it, and you can select multiple games (or all of them) from your libraries at once, before individually selecting your upscaling version preferences in one handy menu (via Techpowerup ). Hit apply, and they all get updated at the same time.
There are many different iterations of DLSS, FSR, and XeSS to choose from, including separate frame generation options and individual upscaler presets. And should a change cause issues, your games can be restored to their original DLLs and preset settings en masse, too.
It's the little things in life, isn't it? This update also adds DLSS Frame Generation Preset C , which is the new beta version that is supposed to significantly boost performance in exchange for a slight drop in visual fidelity. Up to 35% on an RTX 5060, supposedly.
I've had some odd visual results when messing around with different upscaler versions in certain games ( Crimson Desert , I'm looking at you), so the option to easily roll back changes either individually or all at once is a welcome one. I might have a mess around with Preset C later, though, just to see if I can gain a few frames.
A word of warning. DLSS Swapper points out on first boot that messing around with game files could cause some anti-cheat software to flag the changes, so it's probably best to avoid anything with an online component. Lest the banhammer strike for thee.

title: Asus ProArt P16 (H7607) RTX Spark laptop review
text:
If you don't talk to me about the price, I will tell you the Asus ProArt P16 is an unbelievably good gaming laptop. It is beautifully slim, runs incredibly well gaming on battery, and has an absolutely stunning 16-inch OLED screen. And its Arm-based SoC is almost entirely transparent when it comes to running pretty much anything on Windows 11.
But this is no mere Snapdragon device, this the RTX Spark ; Nvidia's first foray into the world of full Windows SoCs. It's pairing a relatively beefy RTX Blackwell GPU with a whole bunch of Arm CPU cores, and doing so with lots and lots and lots of LPDDR5X memory. Y'know, for AI.
Which, er, is why you might not want to ask about that price. Memory's expensive, and these RTX Spark laptops—of which the Asus ProArt P16 is, in my opinion, the most desirable—are likewise brutally priced. I have the 64 GB version, with the top Nvidia N1X SoC inside it, and it will set you back $4,400.
It is that price both for AI and because of AI, and is being sold as the 'One PC' that can do everything. It can game, it can run creative apps, and it can slam through local AI workloads like no other laptop before. But where you're probably expecting me to trot out the old 'jack of all trades, master of none' line here, that's not really the case. There are tradeoffs, sure, but it's really, really good at the lot. And did I mention it was pretty?
The real question here, however, is whether a PC gamer ought to be considering this machine for their next laptop. And if it's just to play games on, this would not be my first choice, however good a device I think it is. The performance, for an Arm-powered laptop, is impressive in terms of the experience, but not faultless. While Microsoft is working hard on Prism and opening up support for every anti-cheat software going, it is not complete. And checking against my back-of-the-napkin list of the 15 biggest PC games around right now you're looking at around half of them not being playable. Yet.
Buy if...
✅ You're a creator or local AI head who games on the side: If you're after an almost workstation style thin and light machine, but also want to play after dark, the ProArt P16 will cover all bases
Don't buy if...
❌ You just want a gaming laptop: There are other thin and light gaming machines that will cost a fraction of what this does, but perform as well in-game.
❌ You have to ask the price: These are machines for the very well-off PC user.

Price

There are many like it, but this one is mine: The 20-core N1X chip, with 10 performance and 10 efficient cores, and the 6144 CUDA core GPU component. This version also comes with a 1 TB SSD (for a $4,400 spec? 😬 I know) and 64 GB of LPDDR5X-9400 memory.
This version of the ProArt P16 is rocking the 16-inch 2880 x 1800 touchscreen OLED display, while there is also a 3840 x 2400 OLED screen available (both 120 Hz) if you go for one of the even pricier models. That one's a touch brighter, but this 1800p OLED will still output at 500 nits, with a 1100 nit peak HDR output, so it's no slouch.
The paucity of storage is a definite disappointment for something at this price—look lower down the stack and you'll still be paying $2800 for the 24 GB version with just a 512 GB SSD. And I honestly do not see the point in that one except for all concerned to be able to say RTX Spark laptops "start from $2800". There is, however, a spare PCIe Gen5 SSD slot in the rear of the machine, which is easily accessible once you remove lots of torx screws.
Future Future The keyboard would be a genuinely lovely thing for this device if I wasn't regularly getting additional keystrokes I did not ask for. I've had to keep deleting the extra spaces this thing keeps adding into my copy. There. I just had to kill another one. It's annoying.
What isn't annoying at all, though, is the glorious, massive haptic touchpad Asus has jammed onto this thing. It quite literally takes up half the width of the device. It's great to the touch, and impressively responsive as your digits glide across its surface. Mmm. Smooth.
It's meant to have a webcam, too, but I cannot for the life of me find out how to turn the damned thing on. I'm assuming that somewhere in there a ribbon cable has become ejected because the device sees nothing. This is what I mean by some quality control issues...
Asus ProArt P16 - Value
Haha. Hahahahahaha. Hahahahahahahahahahahaha.
C'mon. This is the mid-range ProArt P16 for $4,400 . Any sense of value left the station a loooooooong time ago.
Asus ProArt P16 - Sound
(Image credit: Future) This is a very pleasant surprise. The up-firing speakers set either side of the ProArt P16's keyboard are really, really good. Obviously that's still really, really good for laptop speakers, and they're are never going to replace your bookshelf speakers, but for clarity and, yes, even bass they do incredibly well.
And they're loud enough that they can largely overcome the sound coming out of the vents on the ProArt P16 when it's running in full performance mode. It does get rather chatty when the silicon is running at full throttle, and when you're talking about a system that's going to max out its GPU component when running both games and local large language models, that's probably going to happen quite a lot.
The pleasing thing, however, is that knocking things down to the Balanced preset in the ProArt Creator Hub (essentially a reskinned Armoury Crate) means that your performance only drops by a few percentage points but the fan noise drops by a whole hell of a lot. It's not silent—you have to dip into Whisper mode for that—but this is the preset you're going to want to spend most of your time running in.
Asus ProArt P16 - Performance
(Image credit: Future) Somewhat inevitably, performance is a mixed bag of chips when it comes to the RTX Spark. For one, this is a first-gen product from Nvidia, fusing essentially off-the-shelf Arm cores with its own GPU cores, so broad, mature support was never going to be 100% there from the get-go. For another we're talking about games especially that are being run through the Microsoft Prism emulation layer in order for them to run at all on the Asus ProArt P16.
But even taking all that into account I think the gaming performance of this device is pretty damned impressive. The general suggestion ahead of the launch was that the 6144 CUDA core version would deliver gaming performance at a similar level to the RTX 5070 mobile GPUs. It has more cores than the mobile silicon, but is running at a lower clock speed and with a lower power budget, too.
Take a look at the relative 1080p gaming performance of Cyberpunk 2077 and Metro Exodus Enhanced Ed. running on the RTX Spark versus the 100 W Framework 16 or 115 W Razer Blade 14 and you can see where it doesn't quite match up to the GPU performance of the more thirsty graphics parts.

Where there is a clear difference, however, is when it comes to games that are CPU-bound. This is also highlighted in the Cinebench 2024 benchmarks, which show that, while the multi-threaded performance is fine with 20 cores to spread across, the single-core performance is well behind the competition.
Asus ProArt P16 - Aesthetics
(Image credit: Future) Golly, this is a pretty laptop. I know I very much have 'a type', but the ProArt P16 is absolutely nailing the sleek black MacBook aesthetic that works for me. There is a subtle 'ProArt' logo on the lid, just shiny black against the matte black brushed aluminium, and one more etched logo on the bottom left corner of the frame.
And it's also incredibly slim, too. I thought the Blade 14 and Asus Zephyrus G16 were slimline little things, but the ProArt chassis takes it even further. It's super slight, but the brushed aluminium frame makes it perfectly rigid, while remaining lightweight.
But because it's a 16-inch machine, and one without a numpad—which might be a cause for concern for some creatives—the keycaps on the board are wide, so it feels comfortable to type on. I'm also into the big ol' trackpad Asus has used, too, and that OLED panel really makes the whole thing shine.
There is one other thing that has surprised me about the looks of the ProArt P16. After just over a week of solid use there is but a small amount of finger-grease on the spacebar (just because I have to keep hitting the damned thing to try and stop it sticking), but other than that the chassis is remarkably lacking in fingerprints. Normally, this sort of machine is an absolute fingerprint magnet, to the point where you'll want to be carrying around a microfibre cloth in your back pocket just so people don't think you're gross when you whip the laptop out in public.
Instead they may just question your insatiable need to polish up your notebook.
Asus ProArt P16 - Software
(Image credit: Future) The main piece of software to talk about is the OS. Now, this isn't Windows On Arm; that's been effectively retired. This is just plain ol' Windows 11, that just so happens to be running on Arm. And it's impressively transparent as I said earlier. It's slick and feels exactly like running Windows on any other x86 laptop I've used. The only places where you'll notice the difference is in games where they need another level of anti-cheat support the Arm platform doesn't yet offer.
The ProArt P16 does come with a lot of other software, too. You get the aforementioned ProArt Creator Hub, which allows you to alter the power/fan presets, and then there's the MyAsus software where you can register your device and run diagnostics if anything goes wrong. Though I will say it didn't help me track down what was wrong with the webcam because it didn't register its existence, either.
Then you get StoryCube, a piece of software designed to help collate and classify the media on your device using AI. And MuseTree, an app designed for ProArt machines to quickly get you producing AI-generated video and images using local models. You will have to download some extra files/models to actually get up and running, but then you'll be able to run the FLUX.2 model to make your AI dreams a reality.
It's totally offline, so you don't necessarily have to worry about draining reservoirs of water or slamming the energy reserves just to mess around generating a picture of a gaming PC made entirely out of potato, but whether it's really something creatives are going to want to incorporate into their workflows… I am unconvinced.
Given that storage space is at a premium with these RTX Spark machines, I could do without any extra applications installed on my PC, which means there is a bit of cleanup you're going to have to indulge in to claw back the space taken up with pre-installed stuff. But it is all at least relatively unobtrusive. I mean, there's no McAfee pop-ups determined to bug you every 20 minutes unless you sign your life away for some AV cover of dubious virtue.
Asus ProArt P16 - Battery life

I'll be honest, this is one of the real disappointments with the RTX Spark as a laptop platform. The battery life is really not great. With a 99.9 Whr battery inside it, and a relatively power-sipping, efficient platform, I was expecting the battery life to be a lot better than it actually turns out to be.
My expectation was that with an energy efficient Arm SoC I would be happily slapping the lid shut on the ProArt P16 and then flipping it open again ten hours later and it would spring back into life with barely a scratch on the battery capacity. That was effectively my experience from running a Samsung Galaxy Book4 Edge and its Qualcomm Snapdragon chip, and I was hoping to see it replicated.
But no dice. I'm seeing definite power drain when the system suspends, much in the same way as the x86 Ryzen chip in my Blade 14 does.
And then in use it chews through the battery surprisingly quickly, too. I used the PCMark 10 CLI to run the Gaming Battery Life test, which loops 3DMark FireStrike tests until the battery runs dry, and I only got a paltry 86 minutes out of it. That's less than an hour and a half, when the Blade 14 and Framework 16, both with RTX 5070 GPUs, will easily top 130 minutes each.
Now, that is an emulated test, so not quite perfectly set up for this platform, but it's not been inconsistent with my experience actually using this device unplugged. When running a local AI model on Hermes Agent, for example, I've regularly had to plug into a power source while it churns through a tough problem (or sometimes what I thought was a simple one) because running the memory and the GPU at 100% have drained the battery very quickly.
The same is true for gaming, which feels odd given that in Balanced Mode it's running at a total SoC wattage of just over 40 W, and that shouldn't slam through the battery as quickly as it seems to. You can run in Whisper Mode, which cuts the power draw down by a healthy amount again, but then you are running at well under 1000 MHz on the GPU side and it does make gaming a little tougher on the eye.

title: Overwatch's director discusses why King's Row is so iconic, but admits that 'every single map in the game gets a vote'
text:
After Team 4 added map voting to Overwatch one thing became crystal clear: everyone wants to say they're a free thinker who doesn't follow the crowd until King's Row turns up, and then it's a landslide.
King's Row is widely considered to be the best map in Overwatch, I certainly think so. It's one of the few maps that's fun to play on defense and attack, as it doesn't seem overly weighted to either side, at least not until the very end.
(Image credit: Blizzard Entertainment) "There's high ground there, but there's not oppressive high ground," Aaron Keller, game director of Overwatch explained to me after I asked him what, in his mind, made this such an iconic map. "There's areas for a lot of different heroes to do their things. It's fairly tight and close, so you're not going to get out of the action for too long.
"Another thing that I think about a lot with King's Row—sorry this could go on for a really long time—I think that there's something about being able to play through most of the space in a map that I think is just more satisfying for both teams. It can feel really good to hold a team at spawn, but you don't want that every game. You want to feel like it's a close [game]."
As someone who mostly plays support heroes and has put a hell of a lot of time into Ana I can tell you that King's Row is my favourite map thanks to all of its clear sightlines and the fact that tanks never stray too far away from the payload, although the mid stretch can get a bit dicey at times. What I love the most, however, is how you're almost always coming face to face with the enemy providing "big team fight moments" the whole way through the map. But not everyone will agree with me.
(Image credit: Blizzard) "I do think sometimes there can be a sort of agreement that happens as more people vote for King's Row," Keller says. "It just starts to get some momentum there." There are a good deal of people who either vote with what the group wants or just don't vote at all, but every so often players go against the grain.
"Every single map in the game gets a vote," Keller says. "For some people Clash or 2CP is their favourite mode in Overwatch. Even though we think that there's some issues with them, but I think the playerbase is more varied than we think sometimes." I don't doubt that some people love 2CP. Even I wouldn't say I minded it much, although its second objective had some serious issues, which was one of the reasons as to why it ended up getting pulled from the map rotation.
I'm not sure whether Team 4 has tried to recreate the magic that they captured with King's Row, although Neon Junction sort of feels like it but in reverse. But that's alright, because there's plenty of other good maps to be enjoyed, although I know where my voting allegiances lie.

title: I played 20 cozy game demos in Steam Next Fest and these 5 made it onto my wishlist
text:
Fields of Aaru
Release date : TBA
I wasn't keen on the visual style of this ancient Egyptian afterlife farm sim based on its trailers but the low framerate animation and the soft, cohesive environment lighting actually really charmed me once I was hands-on with the demo. The characters have a lot of personality right off the bat and managing hydration to explore the desert is neat too. I also enjoy how, like Roots of Pacha, this one goes for a more abstract currency (memories) and daily objectives instead of high key capitalism.
Farm & Feast
Release date : November 11
I think this cute farming-plus-restaurant sim may click with me the way Travellers Rest didn't. The serving is actually pretty detailed, with making substitutions to menu items on each order, serving drinks, and typing receipt totals into a handset.
Logisticats
Release date : TBA
I really enjoy a chill city builder, but none have grabbed me since Fabledom. Logisticats seems like a real contender though, hitting that same intersection of semi-deep resource management with cute characters.
Beastfolk Barber
Release date : TBA
Think Coffee Talk, but haircuts. It's mostly a visual novel with some hair styling minigames and a "gaining regulars to fulfill a demon bargain" plot. I didn't ever gel with Coffee Talk, actually, but in Beastfolk Barber's demo I was really drawn to the insightful writing about a world where humans live alongside fantasy creatures and all the very real-sounding interpersonal hurdles that entails.
Apple Crumble
Release date : December 3
I always want to get a little cozy horror into the mix and this weird thriller about a dramatic family gathering where someone's got it out for grandma on her 84th birthday looks like a gem. It's like Knives Out if Daniel Craig was a black sheep daughter instead. The full game is planned to only be about 60-90 minutes, the devs say, which is exactly the kind of snack-sized horror story I want.

title: Helldivers 2 studio warns mods may break as it switches to new anti-cheat, and the negative reviews are dropping on Steam like Hellbombs
text:
Heads up, Helldivers: Arrowhead Game Studios is moving Helldivers 2 from GameGuard to Easy Anti-Cheat today, and that means some mods—including those that don't have any impact on gameplay—may stop working.
Helldivers 2 doesn't have official modding support, but there are plenty of them out there —most either cosmetic or audio replacements. Arrowhead said in a Steam update that while it hasn't previously taken a position on mods beyond warning that it can't guarantee their safety or usability, it's seen a recent uptick in cheat mods and it can't let that stand.
"We know mods are part of the DNA of PC gaming and gaming communities as a whole," the studio wrote. "In general, we appreciate the creativity behind cosmetic and non-gameplay mods, which players can enjoy without negatively impacting those who play alongside them.
"Where we need to improve is how we protect players against modifications that create unfair advantages or negatively impact others, which goes beyond software manipulation to tamper with our game."
Thus, two changes are being made:
Additional security measures to crack down on recent cheat mods
Moving from GameGuard to Easy Anti-Cheat on October 20 (that's today) "with additional security tools in place to enhance its effectiveness and improve game integrity protection."
Arrowhead said it's moving to Easy Anti-Cheat because GameGuard "wasn't as effective as it could have been," while EAC is more of an industry standard that should better protect the game. Unfortunately (although also appropriately, given the Helldivers context), there could be some collateral damage in the form of cosmetic mods, some of which may be caught up in the anti-cheat dragnet.
Because mod use in Helldivers 2 "is done at your own discretion," Arrowhead has no advice for what will or won't work, but it invited players to reach out to its support channel on Zendesk if they run into problems they believe are being caused by EAC. The only real fix, though, is to wait for mod makers to update their work.
As you might have anticipated, the move to EAC and its potential impact on mods has not gone over well with the Helldivers community: Since the announcement went up earlier today, more than 1,500 replies have been posted to the Steam discussion thread, and the traditional bombing of the reviews is also underway: 846 negative user reviews have been posted today alone, compared to just 146 positive.

title: Founder of bankrupt Samson studio mulls how to use AI for his next attempt: 'Cutting corners in game development has a habit of coming back to bite you in the ass'
text:
Christofer Sundberg, the founder of Samson developer Liquid Swords, has confirmed the studio's closure, saying that while the console version of the game enjoyed "much greater success" than the PC release, it "wasn't enough to get the company across the finish line."
Reports over the weekend revealed that Liquid Swords had gone bankrupt just six months after the PC release of Samson, which was followed by a console launch in September. "It's been a hell of a ride and a lot of fun, even when the circumstances gave us very little to laugh about," Sundberg wrote. "Building a studio, creating Samson and releasing it on PC and consoles took an enormous amount of work from people who cared deeply about what we were making.
"The console versions met with much greater success than the PC release. We got them out, but that success wasn't enough to get the company across the finish line. Market conditions and some bad business decisions brought us here, and I own my part in that. I can look honestly at what went wrong and still be proud of what we built."
Samson wasn't especially well received when it debuted on PCs, and while post-launch updates have tightened it up, it still holds a very "mixed" rating on Steam , where just 55% of user reviews are positive, and a 51 aggregate score on Metacritic . It wasn't a MindsEye-scale mess, but Sundberg acknowledged shortly after Samson's launch that Liquid Swords " released a game with flaws ."
Sundberg said in his message that discussions about how to support Samson in the future are now underway; more interestingly, he added that, with Liquid Swords gone, he plans to open a new studio. Despite the lack of the traditional cooling-off period, it's not surprising that Sundberg is staying in the game dev biz: Prior to Liquid Swords, he was the co-founder and chief creative officer at Just Cause developer Avalanche Studios.
"We make mistakes, we learn, we fall, we rise up, we move on. That's sometimes a painful process, especially when it affects people you care about, but I refuse to give up. I never give up," Sundberg wrote.
"I'll be back at it again soon and will share more about my plans for a new studio. It will be built with the current market in mind, with a solid foundation and business decisions that give the games and the people making them room to succeed. The lessons from Liquid Swords will be part of how I build it. I still love making games."
It's far too early for anything concrete, but Sundberg told PC Gamer that "starting with what we can actually sustain" is the initial goal.
"A small, experienced team, low running costs and a game we can afford to finish without needing every sales forecast to come true," Sundberg explained. "I want room to make a wrong turn, fix it, and keep going without putting the whole company at risk."
Part of that will include using AI in the development process, "to help with prototyping, repetitive production tasks and testing," Sundberg said—although he emphasized that he doesn't see the technology as a game dev panacea.
"We're not looking to replace roles with AI or treating it as a way to save money (or make money quickly), because AI is bloody expensive too. And cutting corners in game development has a habit of coming back to bite you in the ass. You need solid game development experience to make anything that isn't slop and the proofs are already out there."
You need people who understand the work well enough to know when AI helps and when to switch it off. I'd like us to talk more openly about that.
Christofer Sundberg
Sundberg is also aware of the PR risks attached to AI use, which he believes arise primarily from bold management pronouncements about the "AI-first" future with no consideration of what dev teams actually need or what problems are being solved.
"It feels like everyone is using AI, but hardly anyone talks openly about how," he said. "I think a lot of people are still figuring out where it helps and where it creates more work. Then the bill arrives for all those tokens burned, and they realise it wasn't quite the cheap shortcut they imagined.
"I'm positive about these tools, but 'AI-first' isn't a production plan or a business strategy. You need people who understand the work well enough to know when AI helps and when to switch it off. I'd like us to talk more openly about that."
Alongside the news of Liquid Swords' bankruptcy, there were claims that employees had gone unpaid for at least two months. We have since learned that the studio's bankruptcy means those employees will be paid by Sweden's wage guarantee . Sundberg declined to comment on the possibility of compensation beyond that guarantee, but said "there are people at Liquid Swords [he] would love to work with again," although it's way too soon for any commitments.
"I still want to make games with personality, freedom and enough action to cause a small diplomatic incident," Sundberg said. "I just want the explosions on screen to be bigger than the monthly overhead.
"There's plenty of fight left in me, but the next studio needs to work without running on stubbornness alone. I can do that too, but it's quite exhausting in the long-run."

title: After talking to Capcom, I'm a lot more optimistic about Onimusha 3 getting a remaster
text:
Capcom now makes the majority of its money on PC and "expects this ratio to continue increasing," it said in a report earlier this year—a shift that's been in the works ever since 2018's release of Monster Hunter: World sold approximately three trillion copies. These days Capcom releases a healthy mix of new big budget games and remasters from its back catalog that have never been on PC, like Dead Rising and both Onimusha and Onimusha 2 . The third game in the PlayStation 2 samurai series, co-starring French actor Jean Reno, has always seemed like a bit of a longshot for a remaster given the likely licensing costs and complications around his likeness. But now I have a feeling it's going to happen.
At the end of an interview focused on the series' first new entry in decades, Way of the Sword , I asked Capcom if its sales success has led to new discussions internally about rereleasing 2004's Onimusha 3 or 2006's Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams. And I got a more straightforward answer than I was expecting.
"As series producer, from my position, seeing the reaction to the game and the excitement around it, definitely makes me feel that it would be great to release remasters of Onimusha 3 and Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams," said producer Akihito Kadowaki.
That's not a commitment, of course. Maybe it means nothing at all! But in my experience interviewing Japanese developers, they are usually cautious, caveating statements about unannounced projects with phrases like ' while we can't say anything officially at this time…' or 'I can't speak for the company's future plans, but I personally…' Those sorts of responses usually aren't outright dodging the question, but they remove any real chance that someone would interpret the answer as a promise or even a hint about what the company has coming down the pike.
Kadowaki did frame the answer from his role as the Onimusha series producer, but I still expected a much more circumspect response. Or at least that's what I would expect if remasters weren't already in development. Last year Jean Reno also said he'd be "pleased to reprise his role" , though at what price remains an important question.
But with Capcom's success on PC this decade—heck, even its ancient PC ports like Dino Crisis seem to sell decent numbers—and the clear desire to make Onimusha a going concern again, remastering the rest of the series seems like an obvious way to fill the gap between Way of the Sword and whatever comes next. Maybe we'll be seeing more Onimusha again sooner rather than later.

title: The studio behind Life is Strange, Jusant, and Lost Records: Bloom & Rage is desperately struggling to stay afloat
text:
Things seem to have gone from bad to worse for Don't Nod, the developer of the first two Life is Strange games as well as Jusant, Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden, Lost Records, and Aphelion. A month after saying it might not have enough cash to get through January 2027 and that up to 90 people were at risk of being laid off, the studio has begun "safeguard proceedings" aimed at buying it time while it tries to get its financial situation sorted.
Don't Nod has been struggling since 2024, after both Jusant and Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden, despite being well-received by players and critics, sold " well below expectations ." Work on two new games was put on hold and layoffs followed in 2025, but despite achieving "significant milestones" in its restructuring plan, the studio is still in trouble.
"The videogame industry continues to face an exceptionally challenging environment, marked in particular by highly selective access to financing," Don't Nod CEO and Chairman Oskar Guilbert said in a financial update . "In this context, our current cash position does not allow us to adequately secure all the financing requirements associated with our operations and projects."
Thus the opening of the safeguard proceedings, which Guilbert said "is a proactive, protection measure ... intended to provide the necessary framework and time to build a sustainable solution, while continuing our operations and preserving the value of our assets, our projects and our expertise."
Safeguard proceedings in France, where Don't Nod is based, are a bit like Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the US: Switzerland-based corporate finance advisory firm Hectelion describes it as "a preventive French insolvency procedure available to companies that are not yet in payment default but face difficulties they cannot overcome alone." The process is initiated by the debtor—in this case, Don't Nod—and "provides an observation period of 6–18 months during which creditor enforcement is suspended." During that period, a plan to reduce and reschedule the debt, over a period of up to 10 years, is worked out with creditors and ultimately approved by a court.
Don't Nod may have bought itself some breathing room, but the layoff situation still looks grim. As it said in September, the studio's restructuring plan includes "a refocusing of French operations around a single production line," and that up to 85 people could lose their jobs as a result. Don't Nod also said in the financial update that sales of its latest release, the third-person sci-fi action game Aphelion, "came in below the Group's expectations, weighing on the half-year's performance."

title: My favorite indie roguelike action RPG is tempting me to come back with a transformative new update inspired by Diablo seasons
text:
Hell Clock, one of my favorite indie roguelike action RPGs in the last few years, found a way to take the appeal of limited-time Diablo seasons and make them permanent—no FOMO involved.
Its "Journeys" work much like Diablo and Path of Exile's seasons/leagues by transforming a normal run through the game with new toys to play with, but they won't disappear after a few months. The newest Journey, the Journey of Miracles, is now freely available for anyone who owns the game.
With the Journey of Miracles toggled on, you'll be able to earn powerful buffs for each run whenever you find a statue and survive the juiced up combat encounters they unleash. Some of these Divine Blessings you can grab are absurdly strong, like one that gives you the benefits of a Shrine (eg, extra movement speed, bonus XP gain, etc) by simply drinking a potion. There's a full list of what each one grants you on the Steam page , and I can tell some of them are designed to enable builds that weren't possible before.
Hell Clock isn't quite your typical action RPG. You can equip gear, but the bulk of your character's power comes from their Relics. Every Relic gives you stat bonuses and many of them come with unique effects that change how your abilities work. The Journey of Miracles will introduce several new Relics to the game, some of which bend existing builds in a new direction. I was a fan of the Relic that let me cover the screen in lightning bolts, but I see a new one that juices up their damage in exchange for forcing you to shoot them in a straight line.
In addition to all of that, there's a new underground crypt area with a new miniboss and a long list of patch notes. The Journey of Miracles, like the previous Journey of Nightmares, is completely optional and can be flipped on or off whenever you start a new run through the campaign. You can even play with both enabled if you want to fully embrace the chaos.
I like that there's no rush to blast through all of the new stuff before it disappears. Hell Clock is already a perfect game for playing on and off whenever you have the time to squeeze a run in, and now there's a reason to do it all over again and try a new build or two while you're at it.

title: 'If you can’t show your game to the world without fearing it’ll be cloned, something’s broken' says Moonlighter studio on its canceled demo
text:
Moonlighter and Cataclismo studio Digital Sun Games announced yesterday that it had canceled plans to release a wide public playtest of its forthcoming "tower defensevania" roguelike ReVamp . The reason? The rollout of a more powerful AI model in Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 has led to a surge in hastily turned around clones and decompiles, resulting in thousands of cheap and nasty products flooding Steam and Roblox.
The studio doesn't want people to decompile and steal ReVamp's code. It also wants to prevent opportunists rapidly vibe coding a clone that would hit the market well in advance of ReVamp's March 2027 release date.
While clones have obviously existed forever, for a studio to worry that its concept—and its code —may be pilfered and turned around within days is unprecedented. Digital Sun Games is not the only studio to cancel a demo due to these anxieties.
Digital Sun Games' marketing manager, Israel Mallén, reached out earlier this week to alert me to the demo's cancellation. I shot back a few more questions to get a sense of what the current situation is for a small but experienced dev team.
Scaling a "large playtest" down to a smaller, even more private one must come with marketing / exposure setbacks, right?
Yes, it affects us a lot, mostly in terms of how many people we can actually reach. We had tens of thousands of people signed up for the original Steam playtest. Moving it to Discord means we're looking at a playtest of a few hundred people at best, since we're granting access manually.
Moving to Discord is really about control. We can ask people to sign an NDA, we can see their activity on our server, and we can answer questions live as they play. On Steam, the only lever we have is country-based access. There's no way to vet individual users or tell an active player, someone who buys games, leaves reviews, takes part in forums and other playtests, from an account that was just created for the occasion.
With how fast reverse engineering and recompiling tools have gotten, putting a build in front of that many people this early feels too big a risk. It exposes us to someone lifting the idea, or even shipping something similar to ReVamp before we're ready to launch. You could think that ReVamp's gameplay is a bit more complex than something like an idle or incremental game, but the risk is still there.
We think platforms need to put real protections in place for original work, so developers can keep sharing their games with fans normally.
We'll still do public playtests and demos, just much closer to launch. That means months where we lose the chance to gather feedback at scale and with real players, and get content creators talking about the game. It has a direct impact on how many players we can reach and how visible we are in the market, at a moment where that's already hard enough.
Have you ever worried about quick, opportunistic clones of your demos before this moment, or is it a direct response to the Opus 5.5 avalanche?
We've been making games like Moonlighter and Cataclismo for a decade, and we'd never felt this kind of worry about sharing our games with the community before. If you can’t show your game to the world without fearing it’ll be cloned, something’s broken.
We think platforms need to put real protections in place for original work, so developers can keep sharing their games with fans normally. It's literally how we make a living. In our case, we have the cushion of 250k wishlists and years in the industry behind us, but we're thinking just as much about the developers just starting out. They shouldn't have to make games [while] afraid of this.
Constructing a castle in the "tower defensevania" roguelike ReVamp. (Image credit: Digital Sun) How can Valve and other storefronts combat this?
Honestly, it's hard to say. We don't have the full picture of what storefronts are already doing behind the scenes, and none of this is easy to solve at scale. From where we stand, a couple of things could help. Storefronts are probably in the best position to act, since builds already go through them. On the playtest side, more tools to vet who gets access, like account age, playtime or review history, would let developers keep testing in public more safely. It's complicated, and it will definitely need a lot of input from other devs and companies.
Has this changed the team's attitude towards AI use in game dev?
Well, this situation highlights how new risks are emerging very quickly and without any real control. As an industry, we really need to talk about how to make sure original work is protected.
Where do you see this leading indie game dev in the next six months?
Unless measures are taken, public playtests and demos far from launch will feel risky, especially for games with simpler mechanics or visuals that are easier to replicate. No matter how original or catchy your game is, nothing stops someone from downloading your demo and putting out their own version of it.
If that fear spreads and protections don't arrive, developers will hold back. We'll see fewer public playtests and demos. And when they do happen, they'll be much closer to launch, working more as a marketing tool than as a way to improve the game together with the community.

title: EA Sports FC 27 gets a PEGI 16 rating in Europe because of loot boxes
text:
European game rating agency PEGI has begun increasing its age ratings for games that contain "paid random items," a process that's seeing games initially rated as low as PEGI 3—suitable for all age groups—bounced directly to PEGI 16.
Word of the change came from Connor Hindle, policy manager of the UK's Games Rating Authority. "Since June, newly submitted games have been assessed against an expanded set of criteria within the PEGI rating framework, including new criteria relating to interactive risks," Hindle wrote on LinkedIn (via GamesIndustry ). "As the UK administrator of PEGI, the Games Rating Authority has now begun applying these updated criteria to selected existing digital products."
These changes were announced in March , and are part of PEGI's new "interactive risk categories" that include "purchases of in-game content, paid random items, communication features, and features that incentivise players to continue playing." The new categories reflect the ways we view videogames have changed: While rating systems like PEGI and ESRB were initially created over concerns about violence and sex in videogames, the real dangers turned out to be much more insidious.
As a result, any game with loot boxes is now rated PEGI 16 by default, and that's led to some serious upjumps: EA Sports FC 25, for instance, is rated PEGI 3, as are previous games in the series, but FC 27 is PEGI 16: The former game has "no rating issues," but the newer one has a detailed breakdown of the various purchase options on offer, including FC points, a season pass, and player packs.
(Image credit: PEGI) While PEGI is dropping the rating hammer on loot boxes and other in-game purchases, North America's ESRB has indicated that it will not follow the lead: An ESRB rep said in March that its research indicated that adding "non-content related features" to its rating process could be confusing for parents. EA Sports FC 27 is rated E (Everyone) by the ESRB, with a note that it offers user interactions and in-game purchases.

title: In this age of pervasive slop maybe we should be grateful for Shrek 2 Remastered
text:
Shrek 2 Remastered is coming out in November, it has been announced. I wasn't aware there was a Shrek 2 game for PS2, the OG Xbox, GameCube and PC, probably because in 2004 I was too busy thinking about all the other games coming out. You know, stuff like Half-Life 2, World of Warcraft, Halo 2, Metal Gear Solid 3, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and Wings of Power: WWII Heavy Bombers and Jets.
But Shrek 2 does indeed exist, though contemporary reviews don't point to it necessarily justifying that existence. "You know folks, this game is pretty bad," wrote Nintendo World Report. "Shrek 2 is harmless, inoffensive, middle-of-the-road action for young children," Eurogamer wrote with superlative diplomacy. IGN gave it a 7 even though the reviewer "dreaded" playing it.
It's a 3D platformer, kinda, though it has some interesting features. You can switch between four characters on the go, which clearly inspired Rockstar during the making of GTA 5. It supports local and online co-op for up to four players, which is probably the best way to play it (the original only supported local). There are eleven levels, and apparently they're all quite varied, adopting various moments in the film with aplomb.
It appears to be a port of the PS2 version. The PC version of Shrek 2 was quite different to the console versions, a fact that has caused a bit of fuss in the Steam forums, though a contemporary review from Gamespot notes that "the PC version undercuts that [PS2] title with poor visuals, rougher, shallower gameplay, and an outrageously short running time."
Aspyr Media is handling the port, whose recent work includes the Lord of the Rings: War in the North re-release, and the Neverwinter Nights 2 enhanced edition.
The elephant in the news is that Shrek 2 Remastered releases on November 10, which is nine days before GTA 6. Quite how we'll all be able to wrench ourselves away from this 2004 film-to-game adaptation to suffer Rockstar's latest, I don't know.
Jokes aside: that Shrek 2 was released in 2004 does at least guarantee that humans made it.

title: Here's another gizmo to prevent your graphics card from melting - wouldn't it be nice if 12+4-pin connectors weren't a cause for concern at all?
text:
Power supply manufacturer Super Flower has launched a new accessory that sits between a graphics card and its power cable to ensure neither ends up a hot, expensive mess as too many Nvidia cards seem to be .
It's called the VGA 12+4 pin OCP Dongle . It's a big lump of plastic and ARGB LEDs that measures for high current across the power pins that make up the 12V-2x6 (or 12VHPWR) connector. This connector is capable of delivering up to 600 watts—enough for an RTX 5090 —but it's overcurrent (a current that exceeds the cable/connectors ratings) that could cause a catastrophic failure.
There are really six 'hot' +12V pins on the connector. That means each of those pins needs to carry around 8.33333 amps or thereabouts. That power load doesn't stay perfectly balanced between the pins, due to resistance and imperfections, which means some pins get less amps, while some get more amps. It's when they get a lot more amps that things start to get melty.
Super Flower's OCP Dongle keeps a close watch on those amps, and will indicate when any pin exceeds 9.5 A.
If any one pins is between 9.5 - 12 A, the dongle will light up orange and emit an intermittent buzzing sound.
If any one pin exceeds 12 A, the dongle will light up red and emit a continuous buzzing sound. If this continues for 195 seconds, VGA Black Screen Protection is triggered, which tries to buy you some time to check your connections.
It's a pretty neat solution and one that's not entirely new to me, as I've got something very similar in my own PC: Cooler Master's GPU Shield Adapter Cable . It operates on more or less the same principle, with lights and buzzers to let you know if it's all going to hell in a handbasket.
(Image credit: Cooler Master) That might be a more reliable choice right now, as Uniko's Hardware , who spotted this Super Flower dongle, suggests it is only available in Taiwan right now, included in a bundle with a power supply. There are power supplies that offer similar features, too, such as those with MSI's 'GPU Safeguard+' .
Though why I have to deal with this gnawing worry about my expensive graphics card is another thing entirely. Surely it doesn't have to be this way?

title: Chinese repair centre has received 7 melted 12+4-pin Nvidia GPUs in just the past two days alone
text:
YouTube channel, 修电脑的张哥 , roughly translated to Zhang the Computer Repairman, has posted a video this morning because of the sheer volume of Nvidia GPUs they have had sent in for repair in just the past two days alone. And they're all because of burnt interfaces between the 12+4-pin power cable and the card itself.
Seven cards in total have come in for repair (via Uniko's Hardware ), mostly RTX 5090 cards, along with Asus and MSI RTX 4090. They all come from various manufacturers; as well as Asus and MSI there is also a Gainward card in the mix as well as a Founders Edition RTX 5090 , too.
You can see in the video that either the socket interface is burned, sometimes blackening the PCB, or the 12+4-pin power connector itself has melted into the socket and the user has had to snip the cable off in order to be able to send the card in for testing.
Zhang makes the necessary repairs to each of the cards—removing the interface, cleaning the contacts, and soldering on a new 12+4-pin socket—and then goes ahead and tests each one of them. With the new sockets in place, the repaired cards are back in action and while the GPUs run through some 3DMark benchmarks he checks the temperatures on the cards and the cables.
Some still run a little hot, with the cables at the PSU also running pretty toasty, but nothing particularly worrying at this point.
But still the fact remains that this is a really high volume of cards coming into a single repairshop, all presenting the same symptoms and all from different manufacturers, too. He does also note the users are not necessarily running weak PSUs, and some are even from lab computers (though these might also get hammered more than a card someone is using to game on at home).
It might be that it's a very popular repair channel on BiliBili and YouTube, so potentially he might get sent more than other shops, but it's obvsiously still an issue. It feels like, on a long enough timeline, a whole lot of RTX graphics cards using a 12+4-pin connector are going to suffer from this problem.
(Image credit: YouTube channel 修电脑的张哥) One thing Zhang does note is that during use, if you touch the back of your finger against the power cable, maybe an inch or so above the GPU connector, you should feel it being a little warm. But if it's notably too hot to touch then there's likely an issue.
Likewise he suggests keeping an eye on the power draw via GPU-Z, and particularly the 12+4-pin voltage readout. With failing cards, he notes that if the 12+4-pin voltage drops well below 12 V—to 11.3 or 11.4—then there is likely an issue and you should check the temperature by hand at that point.
What's clear though is this issue isn't going away, isn't purely down to dodgy vendor adaptors or old PSUs, or even miss-aligned cables. The amount of power being drawn by these beefy cards is melting cables and connectors, and if you have one of these GPUs it's worth monitoring it on the regular.
That said, if you want a little more peace of mind, there are new gadgets that can offer some. If not complete protection, then some forewarning of an issue before it becomes a melty mess. Such as this new OCP dongle from Super Flower .

title: 'We expect mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release': Web admins braced for emergency PHP updates to plug leaked high-severity holes
text:
The PHP security team has given advanced notice of an upcoming fix for two critical security vulnerabilities, both rated at 9.2 out of 10 on the CVE severity scale.
Info about the flaws seems to have leaked ahead of their official disclosure, as a video is being shared which reportedly shows a tool called PHP2Shell being used to remotely execute code on webservers via the vulnerabilities (via Ars Technica ).
The PHP programming language is widely used across the internet and powers a huge number of websites. The fix is due to be released at 2pm UTC (10 am ET). Researchers from cybersecurity firm Sansec say the vulnerabilities affect all web servers running PHP 5.4 or later, and that "we expect mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release."
Dane Knecht, the chief technology officer for Cloudflare, says the company is already updating its firewall rules for PHP sites. "We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up. This is a stopgap only," Knecht posted on X . "Patch as soon as @ThePHPF releases the update at 14:00 UTC today."
Speaking to Bleeping Computer yesterday, the CEO of cybersecurity firm WatchTowr, Benjamin Harris, said: "In the last hour, two remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP have been leaked. These vulnerabilities were previously scheduled under embargo and due for release on Thursday at 11 am ET."
(Image credit: Chris Ratcliffe/Bloomberg via Getty Images) "While we are not able to share technical information at this point for obvious reasons, given the sensitivity, we can confirm that these vulnerabilities are indeed real. Both of them are CVSS10 and are understood to affect PHP versions 5, 6, 7, and 8."
It sounds like a pretty anxious time for web administrators around the world right now. The current advice for admins includes taking an inventory of every PHP install, planning a maintenance window to coincide with the update, and making a backup of site and database files in anticipation.
For the rest of us, I guess we're in the hands of the server gods now. 2026 has been a year of increasingly sophisticated security exploits, but this one seems to be on a much larger scale (and of a much higher severity) than most. To quote Samuel L. Jackson in Jurassic Park: Hold on to your butts?

title: 110 million votes later Nurse Harrow has finally made it into Deadlock, with special thanks to a particularly dedicated player who 'cast exactly 1,000 votes for her'
text:
Deadlock's most recent round of hero voting amid the City Never Sleeps release has finally come to an end. First we had the one and only Rat King, then Baba, Solomon, Deadman Danny, Violet, and finally, Nurse Harrow, a support with some unorthodox methods.
From the very beginning I've seen some pretty hardcore Nurse Harrow fans, so I was quite surprised to see her take last place, but Valve has revealed that it wasn't actually that close. 110 million votes were cast in total throughout the entire event with just 22,194 players exclusively voting for Nurse Harrow, however, "one player cast exactly 1,000 votes for her", which shows some real dedication.
(Image credit: Valve) But Nurse Harrow fans have something that no one else in Deadlock has: skill. "Nurse Harrow voters consistently proved to have a higher win rate over all other hero voters." Well I didn't vote for Nurse Harrow and they've read me like a book, so that seems pretty accurate I guess.
Other interesting tidbits concerning the City Never Sleeps voting round include how the closest contest was Baba vs Solomon for second place. I personally voted for Solomon but I wasn't too disappointed seeing how Baba has ridiculously good mobility, melee, and can turn enemies into pigeons. I really love that last one.
It also turns out that I am one of the 36,236 players who voted in every round and never once picked that round's winner, not including Nurse Harrow at the end because she was the last option left. What can I say? I'm just not like other Deadlock players. In my defence, though, only 847 players managed to vote in every single round and pick that round's eventual winner, so the number of oracles that play among us is almost next to none.
I have to admit, seeing the voting come to a close leaves me a little melancholic. Community events like this are massively fun and really well orchestrated in Deadlock, and who knows when we'll get another one. Valve likes to work at their own pace so your guess is as good as mine.
